headline: Production climbs but a hedge loss buries the bottom line
summary_short: Permian Resources' Q1 FY2026 revenue was $1,388.1M, up 0.8% y/y on 11% higher total production, but net income fell 86.7% y/y to $43.6M ($0.05 diluted EPS) after a $339.9M net loss on derivative instruments, mostly non-cash mark-to-market, swamped otherwise-resilient operating income of $467.2M.
summary_long: Oil, NGL and gas volumes rose 10%, 20% and 4% y/y on new/acquired wells, lifting revenue to $1,388.1M despite a 31% NGL price drop and negative $0.29/Mcf gas realizations from weak Waha demand. Operating income was $467.2M, down 7.4% y/y as $52.1M of higher DD&A outpaced revenue growth. A $339.9M net loss on derivatives (mostly non-cash mark-to-market), versus a $57.7M gain a year earlier, drove pretax income down 87.0% y/y to $63.9M. Operating cash flow fell 9.2% y/y to $815.1M, funding $466.2M of drilling capex, $204.9M of bolt-on acquisitions and $134.9M of dividends ($0.16/share). Long-term debt fell 11.3% y/y to $3,546.4M; the company reached investment-grade ratings from S&P and (post-quarter) Moody's. No formal 2026 guidance was disclosed.
